text:
alice: heads up — we're seeing a sudden spike in GPU node failures in sa-east1 (multiple NVLink faults reported). cluster health shows ~35% of GPU pods NotReady. routing is still at region-weight 1.0
ben: confirmed. metrics show increased GPU ECC errors + kernel OOMs starting 09:12 UTC. provisioning queue also backing up.
sre-oncall: I'm on it. initiating autoscale fallback and draining non-critical pools in sa-east1 now. will start traffic migration to us-east1 and eu-west1.
carol: support FYI — we already have two tickets from customers in LATAM complaining about latency/timeouts. I'll prep an initial status page blurb.
support-jen: drafting status update now. suggested text: "We are investigating elevated errors and degraded performance in sa-east1. Traffic is being shifted to alternate regions. No data loss expected. Next update in 30m." ok to post? @alice @ben
alice: post that. include link to active incident bridge and ask customers to DM support for high-priority escalations. add ETA note: "mitigation in progress, expected ~30-45m for traffic stabilization"
sre-oncall: starting canary shift of 10% traffic at 09:22 UTC to us-east1. will monitor latency and error rate.
deploy-bot: [09:22:11] rollout: region-weight change requested by sre-oncall: sa-east1=0.6 -> 0.2, us-east1=0.25, eu-west1=0.15
ben: suggestion — enable permissive CPU fallback for low-priority requests to avoid queue explosion during GPU shortages. this will increase cost but reduce timeouts. approving? @finance-aaron for cost sign-off
finance-aaron: ok for emergency on-demand cross-region usage for this incident. please keep notes on run-hours and estimated spend, we'll reconcile.
carol: status page posted: https://status.redwood.example/incidents/SAE-482 - posted 09:24 UTC. included guidance for customers and contact path for escalations.
support-jen: added canned DM for tier1: "We're actively shifting traffic and monitoring. If you see persistent failures, please escalate and include request IDs."
sre-oncall: canary looks good — error rate dropped ~45% for shifted traffic, latency stable. proceeding to 50% shift.
alice: thanks. please keep transports in place and don't rollback. once shift hits 90% we'll run a health sweep before marking mitigated.
ben: also enabling KV-prefix caching for generation workloads to reduce token load while GPUs stabilize.
sre-oncall: shift at 09:34 UTC now at 78%. we hit a hiccup on one cross-region peering link — packet loss ~2% — rerouting around it.
deploy-bot: [09:35:02] alert: cross-region peering path switched by net-controller to path-b
carol: customer escalation — enterprise acct "MapleHealth" opened a priority ticket asking for ETA. support-jen is on the call with them.
support-jen: on call with MapleHealth, gave ETA 30m for full stability, offered temporary token whitelist to avoid retries.
alice: note for postmortem: root cause looks like a firmware bug in 2 node families causing NVLink flaps under sustained load. collect kernel logs, nvlink counters, and preflight outputs.
ben: capturing logs now: command I used: ``kubectl -n infra logs -l nodepool=sa-gpu --since=1h | gzip > /tmp/sa-gpu-logs.gz``
sre-oncall: mitigation timeline: 09:22 start traffic shift -> 09:40 90% shift target achieved -> 10:05 complete post-shift sweep and begin partial restart of affected pools -> 10:20 estimated complete. I'll update status page at each milestone.
support-jen: posted interim update on status page with new ETA 10:20 UTC and contact instructions.
alice: once we confirm stabilization, we'll communicate more detailed impact and customer-specific notes. thanks all — keep messages short here, escalate off-thread when needed.
sre-oncall: final check at 09:52 UTC — core P95 latency back within normal for shifted traffic. continuing to monitor for 30m before closing.
carol: escalations tracked: MapleHealth (on call), two mid-market customers in BR - both notified and offered workarounds.
ben: cost estimate so far: additional on-demand GPU hours ~12 GPU-hours, temporary CPU fallback ~40 vCPU-hours. rough delta $1.2k. finance-aaron, will detail in incident cost report.
finance-aaron: acknowledged, thx.
sre-oncall: marking incident as "mitigated" in the internal tracker at 10:22 UTC. will keep monitoring.
alice: closing note: please attach all logs to the postmortem and add any customer comms drafts to the incident doc. great response everyone. :thumbsup:
